C Major Scale on Guitar: 3 Positions, String by String

The C major scale contains C D E F G A B. Start with frets 0–3, including open strings, then explore the positions around the roots at fret 3 on string 5 and fret 8 on string 6.

Notes and degrees

NoteDegreeSemitones from root
CR (root)0
D2 (major 2nd)2
E3 (major 3rd)4
F4 (perfect 4th)5
G5 (perfect 5th)7
A6 (major 6th)9
B7 (major 7th)11

Starting the C major notes on D gives D Dorian. The seven notes stay the same, but their degrees change because the root changes.

Full fretboard

Each circle shows a degree, with its note name below. Roots are labeled R and highlighted in amber. Fret 0 is an open string.

Frequently asked questions

What are the notes of C major?
The seven notes are C D E F G A B. The notes table pairs each note with its degree and distance from the root.
Where is the root?
Find C at fret 3 on string 5 and fret 8 on string 6. Root markers are labeled R and highlighted.
What is the step pattern?
The pattern is whole, whole, half, whole, whole, whole, half.
